title: AI Solves 56-Year-Old Unresolved Mathematical Problem, Landmark Peer-Reviewed Research Published in Science by DeepMind
source_used: 36Kr (text from QbitAI, published with authorization); cross-checked with The Decoder, 12 Oct 2026
key_facts: DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus, a Gemini-powered agent framework for mathematical proof, is the subject of a peer-reviewed study published in Science.
It solved 9 open Erdős problems out of 353 it attempted (problems that already had formal Lean versions); two of the nine had been open for 56 years.

It also proved 44 conjectures from the OEIS integer-sequence database, solved a 15-year-old algebraic geometry question (log-concavity of Hilbert functions) and improved a theoretical bound in convex optimization.
Workflow: Gemini 3.1 Pro writes proofs, the Lean checker verifies them, error reports go back to Gemini, repeat until the proof passes.

The simplest configuration (Gemini plus Lean feedback, no AlphaProof or evolutionary search) also solved all nine Erdős problems; the full version was about 2 to 5 times more cost-effective on the hardest ones.
Cost is roughly several hundred dollars per problem; the full set of Lean proofs has been made public.
Two mathematicians (Carnegie Mellon University and the University of South Carolina) published a comment in the same Science issue titled 'AI for mathematical research has arrived'.

36Kr sets this against OpenAI's release of 722 mathematical proofs, which drew pushback from mathematicians; The Decoder says OpenAI put hundreds of AI proofs on GitHub instead of submitting them to journals.
quote_evidence: It solved 9 Erdős open problems, two of which had remained unsolved for a full 56 years.
The full set of Lean proof codes from this project has been made public, and the public can view them directly.
